items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: Victor Young said there was a wonderful gentlemen by the name of Albert Coates... And Victor Young said, 'If you had any brains you’d go take some conducting lessons right now.'

ctx.x: Time. And then Victor Young said there was a wonderful gentlemen by the name of Albert Coates who was a conductor in the period of Thomas Beecham in England, and he was driven out of England by Beecham with his wealth. And he formed an orchestra for the Czar before the royal family in Russia was done away with. And there are still records with him, Coates, and he was a great, great conductor. And Victor Young said, “If you had any brains you’d go take some conducting lessons right now. Maybe you won’t learn…
Those clicks, did they work on the quarter note? Were you hearing the quarter note or were your hearing something different?
